Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for 3-day constant severe headache with photophobia and visual disturbance; suspected migraine. Plan for in-person neurological and eye exam, start stronger NSAID with acetaminophen, safety-net advice provided.

History:
- Presenting complaint: “Blinding” headache for 3 days, started suddenly on waking; constant; partially relieved by ibuprofen but persistent.
- Symptom details:
  - Location: Diffuse, worse over right eye.
  - Severity: ~8/10, reduced to ~5/10 with ibuprofen.
  - Associated: Photophobia; intermittent “shooting light”/visual disturbance; mild nausea without vomiting; increased fatigue; stabbing pain when standing quickly or moving head.
  - Sleep: Able to sleep; not waking from headache; can wake with headache in the morning.
  - No fever (not checked), no URTI/sinus symptoms, no cough/hemoptysis, no weight change, no focal neurologic symptoms (no tingling/numbness/weakness), no change in smell/taste.
- Past headaches: Occasional brief headaches previously, responsive to ibuprofen; no prior visual symptoms, nausea, or vomiting with past headaches.
- Past medical history: Non-contributory per patient (mentions past pain in youth, no cause found).
- Medications:
  - Combined oral contraceptive pill (exact name/dose not documented); started ~1 year ago; no noted side effects; no perceived change in headache frequency until current episode.
  - Ibuprofen as needed for headache (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Family history: Mother has migraines with vomiting.
- Social history:
  - Lives alone; works from home; reduced ability to work over past 3 days (missed part/all of work).
  - Tobacco: No.
  - Alcohol: Drinks weekly; exact amount unclear in transcript.
  - Recreational drugs: No.
- Preventive/other:
  - Recent eye exam: “Normal.”
  - BP reportedly normal at pharmacy when starting pill (about 1 year ago).
  - No recent travel.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Physical exam: Not performed (telehealth); plan for in-person neurological exam and fundoscopy.

Impression:
- New-onset severe headache with photophobia and visual disturbance; probable migraine. Requires in-person neurological and fundoscopic evaluation and blood pressure check. Consider contraceptive review if migraine with aura is confirmed.

Plan:
- Medication:
  - Prescribed a stronger NSAID similar to ibuprofen (name/dose/route/frequency not documented); take with food.
  - May take acetaminophen concurrently (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Evaluation:
  - Book in-person appointment via support team for full neurological exam, fundoscopy, and blood pressure measurement.
- Contraception:
  - If migraines with flashing lights (aura) are confirmed/recurrent, combined oral contraceptive may be unsuitable; consider alternative contraception at review. Continue current pill for now.
- Safety net:
  - If headache becomes unbearable, worsens, or changes, go to the emergency department; may contact clinic for further advice.
  - If symptoms resolve before the appointment, cancellation is acceptable.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Full medication list and doses; vitals; neurological exam; fundoscopy; visual acuity/pupil exam; neck stiffness assessment; pregnancy status; detailed alcohol quantity; exact NSAID prescribed with dose/route/frequency; acetaminophen dose/route/frequency; name of contraceptive pill.
- Internal conflicts: None noted; alcohol quantity unclear due to transcript.
- Transcript quality: Several inaudible/redacted sections; some responses unclear; patient identifiers not captured.
